Guess an assay type from the values

Source: R/class-omics_input.R
infer_assay_type.Rd

A starting point for an import wizard, not a verdict: it separates linear proteomics intensities from already-transformed ones by magnitude, the same heuristic check_assay_scale() uses, and assumes counts for RNA-seq because that is what gets uploaded. The caller is expected to show the guess and let the user correct it – nothing else recovers the scale if this is wrong.

Usage

infer_assay_type(expr_mat, omics_type)

Arguments

expr_mat

Expression matrix.

omics_type

Omics modality.

Value

A single assay type from SUPPORTED_ASSAY_TYPES, or NA_character_ for a modality with no vocabulary.

See also

Other omics_input: LOG_SCALE_ASSAY_TYPES, SUPPORTED_ASSAY_TYPES, check_assay_scale(), drop_meta_na(), is_omics_input(), normalize_omics(), omics_input(), select_complete_cases(), subset_omics(), subset_omics_features(), subset_omics_samples(), summarize_omics(), validate_omics_input()

Examples

infer_assay_type(matrix(2^rnorm(40, 20, 2), nrow = 10), "proteomics")
#> [1] "raw_intensity"
infer_assay_type(matrix(rpois(40, 200), nrow = 10), "rnaseq")
#> [1] "raw_count"
